Tetapkan aturan role versus tier akses.
Tetapkan aturan reset, retensi riwayat, dan sertifikat.

Eksekusi Test Cases lalu catat bukti dan Defect ID.
Gunakan Execution Log untuk retest dan siklus berikutnya.
Unauthenticated user opens dashboard or course URL

1. Open the LMS URL.
2. Open a protected URL directly.
User is redirected to /login and receives a clear login-required message. No protected data is rendered.

1. Open login.
2. Enter valid credentials.
3. Submit.
Login succeeds and the user is routed to the dashboard permitted for the account type.
Valid credentials create an authenticated session.

1. Enter an unknown username.
2. Enter a password.
3. Submit.
Login is rejected with a clear, non-sensitive error. No session is created.

1. Enter a registered identity.
2. Enter the wrong password.
3. Submit.
Login is rejected with a clear, non-sensitive error. No session is created.
Submit login with required fields empty

1. Leave one or more required fields blank.
2. Submit.
Client/server validation identifies the required field and prevents submission.
Required login fields must be completed.

1. Enter valid credentials.
2. Enter an incorrect captcha.
3. Submit.
Login is rejected and a clear captcha error is shown. Captcha state is refreshed or remains valid according to the defined rule.

1. Refresh the captcha or wait until expiry.
2. Submit using the old value.
Old/expired captcha is rejected and the user can obtain a new captcha.
Captcha has a defined lifetime and refresh behavior.
Account exists and rate-limit policy is configured
Wrong password repeated according to policy

1. Submit invalid credentials repeatedly.
2. Observe account and response behavior.
Rate limiting or lockout follows the configured threshold, does not expose account existence unnecessarily, and provides recovery guidance.

1. Click Logout.
2. Reopen the dashboard URL.
Session is invalidated and protected pages require login again.

1. Login.
2. Remain idle until timeout.
3. Request a protected page.
User is redirected to login. Protected data is not accessible after timeout.
Idle sessions expire according to policy.
User logged in and has visited a protected page

1. Open a protected page.
2. Logout.
3. Press Back and refresh.
Cached content is not usable; refresh requires authentication and does not expose protected data.
Logged-out users cannot reuse cached protected content.
User attempts protected API or asset URL directly
Low-access account; protected API or asset URL

1. Login as a user without access.
2. Request the protected endpoint/resource directly.
Server-side authorization rejects the request and does not disclose the protected content, even if the UI hides the item.
Authorization is enforced at the server/resource layer.
Basic and Premium test accounts and courses are configured
Basic account; Premium account; catalog snapshot

1. Login as Basic.
2. Record visible courses.
3. Login as Premium.
4. Record visible courses.
Each account sees exactly the courses allowed by its configured tier.
Course catalog is filtered by entitlement.
Restricted course is hidden or clearly marked

1. Open the catalog.
2. Search for the restricted course.
Course is hidden or marked unavailable with a defined call to action; no unauthorized content is exposed.
Restricted content has a consistent discoverability rule.

1. Login with an account without access.
2. Open the course URL directly.
Access is rejected with the defined 403/access-denied behavior or upgrade guidance; course data is not shown.
Direct URL manipulation cannot bypass entitlement checks.

1. Open the course.
2. Click Mulai Belajar/Enroll.
3. Open Materi Saya.
Enrollment succeeds, the course appears in Materi Saya, and the initial progress is recorded correctly.
Same course; repeated click or repeated request

1. Enroll.
2. Repeat the action or refresh during submission.
Only one enrollment is created; the UI and backend remain consistent.
Enroll in unpublished or inactive course
1. Try to open or enroll in the course.
User cannot enroll; the course is hidden or shows the defined unavailable message.
Only eligible published courses can be enrolled.
Progress updates after completing an activity
User enrolled in a course with measurable activity progress

1. Open an activity.
2. Complete it according to the completion rule.
3. Return to the course/dashboard.
Activity status and overall progress update accurately and persist after refresh.
Resume course after refresh or relogin

1. Complete part of an activity.
2. Refresh, logout, and login again.
3. Reopen the course.
Progress is preserved and the user can resume from the correct state.
User has partial progress and access to a second browser/device

1. Make progress in client A.
2. Open the course in client B.
The defined synchronization behavior is met without overwriting newer progress incorrectly.
Course has a prerequisite activity sequence
Attempt to open a later locked activity

1. Enroll.
2. Try to open an activity before its prerequisite.
Access is blocked or allowed according to the configured prerequisite rule, with a clear explanation.
Published course has Pre-Test, Quiz, Literatur, Zoom, Assignment, and Video activities
Reference course with all activity types

1. Enroll.
2. Open course detail.
3. Review the activity list.
All required activities appear in the configured order with correct names and types.
Course detail reflects the published curriculum.
Course contains incomplete, in-progress, and completed activities
Status fixture for each activity state

1. Open course detail.
2. Inspect each activity status.
Each activity shows the correct status and status changes after completion.
Activity status is visible and accurate.
Instructions, question count, timer, and start state are displayed correctly.
Published tests can be started by eligible users.

1. Open Quiz.
2. Answer several questions.
3. Navigate between questions.
Answers are captured, navigation behaves as designed, and selected answers remain visible.
Leave at least one question blank

1. Start quiz.
2. Leave one or more questions blank.
3. Submit.
System follows the configured rule: blocks submission with clear guidance or submits and marks unanswered questions correctly.
Unanswered questions have a defined submission rule.

1. Start the quiz.
2. Observe countdown at start, middle, and near zero.
Countdown is visible, progresses from the server-defined start time, and does not reset unexpectedly.
Quiz timing is accurate and server-authoritative.

1. Start quiz.
2. Let timer reach zero without submitting.
System auto-submits or closes according to policy, records the attempt exactly once, and stores the correct score/status.
Quiz answer key and scoring rule are configured

1. Submit a quiz with known answers.
2. Review result.
Score is calculated from the configured answer key and displayed/stored correctly.
Quiz scoring is automatic and accurate.
Scores at threshold minus one, threshold, and threshold plus one

1. Execute attempts with each boundary score.
2. Review pass/fail status.
Status matches the exact configured boundary rule, including equality at the threshold.
Refresh or browser close during quiz
Quiz supports or disallows resume according to policy

1. Answer some questions.
2. Refresh or close the browser.
3. Reopen the quiz.
System resumes, discards, or submits according to the defined rule without corrupting the attempt.
Interrupted attempts have a defined recovery rule.

1. Complete quiz.
2. Click Submit repeatedly or resend the request.
Only one result and one attempt are recorded.
Read or download valid literature PDF

1. Open literature activity.
2. View/download the file.
PDF opens or downloads successfully, remains readable, and completion status follows the configured rule.
Published literature is accessible to eligible users.
Test fixture contains a missing or unavailable file

1. Open the activity.
2. Attempt to view/download.
A friendly error is shown; the user is not presented with a broken or misleading completion state.

1. Open video activity.
2. Play, pause, seek, and resume.
Video controls work, playback is stable, and progress/completion follows the configured watch rule.
Training video is playable and trackable.
Seek to near end without watching full content

1. Open the video.
2. Seek directly near the end.
3. Observe completion state.
Completion status follows the configured threshold and cannot be bypassed unexpectedly.
Video completion is controlled by an explicit rule.
Zoom activity has a valid link and future schedule

1. Open Zoom activity.
2. Inspect schedule.
3. Click the meeting link.
Schedule is displayed in the correct timezone and the link opens the intended destination.
Assignment with allowed formats and deadline

1. Open assignment.
2. Review instructions and constraints.
Instructions, allowed formats, maximum size, and deadline are visible and consistent with configuration.
Assignment constraints are communicated to the participant.

1. Complete an activity.
2. Check in-app/email notification according to policy.
Notification is sent once with the correct course/activity and status.
Activity events trigger the configured notification.
Assignment is open and accepts PDF

1. Open assignment.
2. Upload PDF.
3. Click Kirim Tugas.
File uploads successfully, status becomes Terkirim/Menunggu Penilaian, and confirmation is shown.
Valid allowed file can be submitted.
Assignment is open and accepts DOCX
File uploads successfully and appears in the submitted assignment record.
Allowed document formats are accepted consistently.
EXE, MP4, or other unsupported format
File is rejected before or during upload with a clear format message; no invalid record is created.
Only configured extensions/MIME types are allowed.
File exactly at the configured limit, such as 2 MB if configured

1. Select a file exactly at the limit.
2. Submit.
File is accepted if the rule is inclusive and the recorded size is correct.
Maximum file size boundary is explicit.
File slightly larger than the configured limit

1. Select a file just above the limit.
2. Submit.
File is rejected with a clear size message and no incomplete orphan upload remains.
Upload corrupted file with allowed extension
System rejects the file or marks it unusable according to policy without claiming a valid submission.
File content is validated, not only the extension.

1. Submit file A.
2. Replace/resubmit with file B.
The allowed resubmission rule is enforced, the latest/approved version is clear, and status/history remain consistent.
Assignment deadline is in the future

1. Upload valid file before deadline.
2. Submit.
Submission succeeds and records the correct timestamp.

1. Open assignment after deadline.
2. Attempt upload/submit.
Submission is blocked or labeled late according to the configured policy; UI and backend agree.

1. Start upload.
2. Interrupt connection.
3. Restore connection and inspect status.
No false success is shown; user receives a retry path and no corrupted submission is recorded.
Upload failures are recoverable and visible.

2. Try to open Post-Test.

2. Submit a failing Post-Test attempt.
Attempt is recorded as failed, score is stored, and retry/reset state follows policy.
Post-Test score exactly at pass threshold
Attempt score exactly equal to threshold
1. Submit a score equal to the configured threshold.
System marks the user Passed if the rule is inclusive; certificate eligibility updates accordingly.
Pass threshold equality rule is explicit.
First and second failed attempts can be retried
Retry policy allows up to three attempts

1. Fail attempt 1.
2. Start attempt 2 and fail.
3. Observe action buttons and count.
Attempt count increments correctly and the next attempt is available if policy allows.
Two previous failed attempts; third attempt allowed

1. Submit a passing third attempt.
2. Inspect course status and certificate eligibility.
User is marked Passed; no reset occurs; certificate flow becomes available if other requirements are met.
Passing on the last allowed attempt is successful.
Two previous failed attempts; third attempt allowed

1. Submit a failing third attempt.
2. Inspect course and user status.
User is marked Tidak Lulus Materi and the exact configured reset/lockout rule is executed.
Three failed attempts trigger the defined consequence.
At least one failed attempt recorded

1. Complete a failed attempt.
2. Refresh and relogin.
3. Reopen Post-Test.
Attempt count and available actions remain correct after session changes.

Course with progress, scores, and submission

2. Inspect progress, activity states, and course action.
Only the fields defined by policy are reset, progress is set to the defined value, and the course is restartable or locked as specified.

Reset of scores and assignment state
Prior Pre-Test/Quiz scores and submitted assignment

2. Trigger reset.

2. Interrupt or observe the operation.
3. Reload the course.

2. Check in-app/email notification.

values: Test case lengkap berdasarkan dokumen uji fungsi Umum, Admin, dan Pemateri, ditambah boundary, security, recovery, dan cross-cutting checks yang diperlukan agar siap dipakai untuk UAT.
Authentication, authorization, catalog/course access, enrollment, learning activities, quiz, assignment, Post-Test/reset, certificate, time limit/expiry, Admin, Pemateri, dan quality checks.
Mulai dari Summary. Jalankan test case pada Test Cases. Isi Status, Tester, Execution Date, Actual Result, Evidence, dan Defect ID. Gunakan Execution Log untuk siklus uji berulang.
Nama role, tier akses, ekstensi file, batas ukuran, nilai kelulusan, masa aktif, zona waktu, dan aturan reset harus disesuaikan dengan requirement resmi sebelum eksekusi.
Not Run, Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not Applicable
Critical = berpotensi memblokir rilis atau menyangkut akses/data/kelulusan; High = alur utama; Medium = fungsi pendukung; Low = minor.
Traceability menunjukkan cakupan requirement dan test case. Coverage ‘Covered’ berarti test case telah dibuat, bukan berarti telah lulus.

Tetapkan role versus subscription tier; aturan reset dan retensi riwayat; daftar format file; batas ukuran inklusif/tidak; pass threshold; timezone; notification channel; publication lifecycle; dan metrik keberhasilan.
